events.text: After a game, a private message from an account you do not know: "{coach}, I coach an academy team. Your aim is fine. Your second round after a lost pistol is a disaster. Want the demo review?"

choices.text: Say yes and take notes for two hours
choices.result: It hurts, and every word is true. {coach} ends with: "Send me a demo every month."

choices.text: "My Elo says I am doing fine."
choices.result: "Elo is not a team sport, kid." He does not write again.

events.text: {elo} Elo. You enter the top 500 of your region, where the same fifty names queue every night, some of them pros on their day off.

choices.text: Play your role and let the pros do their thing

win.text: A pro you have watched for years says "nice flash" in voice. You replay it in your head all week.

lose.text: At this level every mistake is punished within two seconds.

choices.text: Take every duel against them. That is why you are here

win.text: You out-aim a tier 1 player three rounds in a row. Someone clips it.

lose.text: They read you like a tutorial.

events.text: An academy team runs open tryouts this weekend: two days of scrims, forty candidates, one contract.

choices.text: Show up and play like it is a final

win.text: You make the last five. No contract yet, but your name is now in a scout's spreadsheet.

lose.text: Cut after day one. You learned what the level really is.

choices.text: Skip it. Forty candidates is a lottery
choices.result: You spend the weekend in queue instead.

events.text: A friend says you should stream your FACEIT games: "Level 10 at your age, people would watch."

choices.text: Go live with a webcam and talk through every round
choices.result: Forty viewers, then two hundred. Talking while playing costs you a few rounds.

choices.text: Stream with no camera, no voice, just the game
choices.result: A few regulars come for the crosshair placement.

choices.text: No. The game first
choices.result: Nobody knows your face. Everybody in your lobbies knows your name.

events.text: Final exams in three weeks. An online qualifier with your mix team falls on the exact same days.

choices.text: Exams first. The team finds a stand-in
choices.result: You pass. Your parents stop counting your hours for a while.

choices.text: Do both and sleep in July

win.text: You pass the exams and reach the last round of the qualifier. Nobody knows how.

lose.text: You scrape through the exams and throw the deciding map, half asleep.

choices.text: The qualifier. School can wait a year
choices.result: You play well. The conversation at home is harder than any match.

events.text: A friend at level 6 begs you to play on his account for an evening to get him out of "Elo hell".

choices.text: No. Coach him through his own games instead
choices.result: Explaining why you rotate teaches you why you rotate.

choices.text: One evening cannot hurt

win.text: Nobody notices. You feel a bit dirty and promise yourself it was the last time.

lose.text: Account sharing is against the rules: his account gets flagged and yours gets a warning.

events.text: Loading screen: on the other team, {star} from {rival}, playing a casual FACEIT game on stream with 20,000 viewers.

choices.text: Play the best game of your life

win.text: You top frag. On stream, {star} checks your profile and says: "He is how old?"

lose.text: Your hands are cold all game. Twenty thousand people watched you whiff.

choices.text: Treat it like any other game
choices.result: A normal game, a normal win. You only check the stream VOD twice.

events.text: Before your first Major, an email from the organisers: "Please send your autograph for the player sticker capsule." A share of every sticker sold goes to you. You have one white page and a marker.

choices.text: A clean, readable signature
choices.result: It looks good on an AK. Your mother buys one.

choices.text: Add a tiny drawing that will become your trademark

win.text: The community loves the little doodle. Your sticker outsells half the playoff teams.

lose.text: It prints as a blob. "What is it?" becomes a meme, a friendly one.

events.text: Media day at {tournament}. Six hours of photos, slow-motion walks and the same three questions in front of a green screen. Your first match is tomorrow.

choices.text: Give the cameras everything: poses, jokes, the stare
choices.result: Your intro video is the one the broadcast plays before every match.

choices.text: Do the minimum and save your energy
choices.result: Arms crossed, one take. Back to the practice room by noon.

events.text: {tournament}. You play the home team. Twelve thousand people boo your name during the introductions, and they have not even seen you play yet.

choices.text: Cup your ear at the crowd and smile

win.text: You feed on it. Every round you win, the arena gets quieter. By the end, some of them clap.

lose.text: You asked for noise. You get it after every round you lose.

choices.text: Headset on, eyes on the monitor, nothing exists

win.text: White noise. You play it like an online match.

lose.text: You can feel the floor shake through the chair.

events.text: {tournament}. Somewhere in the stands, a group of fans has made a banner with your name and your crosshair on it. They start a chant during the tech pause.

choices.text: Stand up and wave at them
choices.result: The section explodes. You will sign that banner after the match.

choices.text: Stay in your bubble, thank them after
choices.result: You find them at the exit, an hour later. They did not expect that.

events.text: {tournament}. Two losses in two matches. One more and you fly home. At the hotel, nobody wants to be the first to speak.

choices.text: "We need three wins. Others have done it. Why not us?"

win.text: Something shifts in the room. Tomorrow you play with nothing to lose.

lose.text: The speech sounds like a film. Nobody believes it, including you.

choices.text: No speech. Order pizza and put a comedy on
choices.result: Nobody talks about Counter-Strike until breakfast. It helps.

choices.text: Review both losses until 3 a.m.
choices.result: You find the leak. You also find the bottom of the coffee machine.

events.text: The Pick'Em predictions are public: most viewers have picked your team to go out 0-3. Someone prints the graph and tapes it to the practice room door.

choices.text: Leave it there. Free motivation
choices.result: Everyone touches the sheet on the way out, like a lucky charm in reverse.

choices.text: Post it yourself: "Sorry for your Pick'Em."

win.text: You back it up on the server. The post ages like fine wine.

lose.text: The replies are waiting for you after the loss. Thousands of them.

events.text: {tournament}, 11-10 for you. A technical pause that lasts twenty-five minutes. Your hands are cooling down and the momentum is draining away.

choices.text: Keep the team talking about the next two rounds

win.text: When the game resumes, you are the only team still in the match.

lose.text: Too much talk. You over-think the first round back.

choices.text: Hand warmers, jokes, no tactics
choices.result: The admin has to ask you to stop laughing so loudly.

events.text: {tournament}. Across the stage sits {star} of {rival}, whose poster was on your bedroom wall. He nods at you during the sound check.

choices.text: Nod back. Today he is just another opponent

win.text: You win your duels against him. At the handshake he says: "You are for real."

lose.text: You hesitate on every peek against him. He is still very, very good.

choices.text: Tell him about the poster
choices.result: He laughs and asks you to sign his mousepad after the match, "for when you are famous".

events.text: Your parents are in the arena for the first time. The same parents who used to switch the router off at 22:00. The camera finds them in the crowd before the match.

choices.text: Play for them

win.text: After your clutch, the broadcast cuts to your father on his feet, shouting a callout he does not understand.

lose.text: You want it too much. They hug you just the same.

choices.text: Forget they are there until the last round
choices.result: You find them after the match. Your mother asks why everyone was shouting "banana".

events.text: You have just won. A microphone, a full arena, and the interviewer's question: "A word for your next opponent?"

choices.text: "Respect to them. May the best team win."
choices.result: Polite applause. Clean.

choices.text: "Tell them to pack light. It is a short trip."
choices.result: The arena roars. The clip is everywhere within the hour. Now you have to win.

choices.text: Give the microphone to the teammate who carried the map
choices.result: He was not ready. He will remember it all his life.

events.text: The night before the biggest match of your career. It is 1 a.m. and you are staring at the hotel ceiling, replaying rounds that have not happened yet.

choices.text: Get up and do thirty minutes of deathmatch to empty your head
choices.result: Your hands remember what to do. You fall asleep at 2.

choices.text: Breathing exercises from the mental coach

win.text: Four seconds in, six out. You do not remember the tenth breath.

lose.text: You count breaths until 4 a.m.

choices.text: Knock on a teammate's door. He is not sleeping either
choices.result: Two hours of talking about everything. You will both remember this more than the match.

events.text: The bracket is out. On the other side of the stage: {rv}, the player who has followed you since your FACEIT days. He posts a photo of the draw with one word: "Finally."

choices.text: Reply: "Bring a pen. You will want my autograph."

win.text: You win the duel that decides the map and point at his side of the stage. The story of the tournament.

lose.text: He gets you three times in a row and mimes signing an autograph.

choices.text: Like the post and say nothing
choices.result: Ten years of history, settled on the server and nowhere else.

events.text: A fan waits two hours at the players' exit with a printed screenshot of your best round and a silver pen. Your shuttle leaves in three minutes.

choices.text: Sign it, take the photo, miss the shuttle
choices.result: You walk back to the hotel. His post about it reaches more people than your match did.

choices.text: A quick signature through the window
choices.result: Ten seconds. He looks at the paper all the way home.

events.text: {tournament}, Dust II. 1v2, you have the bomb and you are alone at Long A, 35 seconds left. One CT is somewhere on site, the other was last seen at B.

choices.text: Smoke the cross, plant for Long and hold from Pit

win.text: They have to come to you one by one. Two taps from Pit. The arena erupts.

lose.text: The site CT was hiding at Goose. He kills you on the plant.

choices.text: Swing wide onto the site and take the first duel now

win.text: One. Then the rotation runs straight into your crosshair. Two.

lose.text: You win the first duel at 12 HP. The second CT finishes it.

choices.text: Save the rifle. The economy matters more
choices.result: You drop the bomb in Pit and walk away. Next round you have an AK.

events.text: {tournament}, Mirage. 5v4 retake on A, the bomb is planted for Default with 30 seconds left. You are in Jungle with one smoke and one flash. Three teammates are coming through CT.

choices.text: Smoke Stairs, flash over the site and call the go on your pop

win.text: Perfect pop. Three kills in two seconds, defuse with time to spare.

lose.text: The flash pops early and blinds CT. The retake dies in the open.

choices.text: Peek Connector alone first to get an opening kill

win.text: You catch the lurker looking the wrong way. 5v3, the rest is easy.

lose.text: He was waiting. 4v4 now, without your utility.

choices.text: Wait for everyone and trade your way in

win.text: Slow, ugly, effective. Defused with 0.4 seconds left.

lose.text: Too slow. The bomb goes off as your teammate holds the defuse.

events.text: {tournament}, Inferno, CT side. It is 11-11 and they have rushed Banana three rounds in a row. You hold B with one teammate, an incendiary and a smoke.

choices.text: Throw the incendiary deep at Car and fight for Banana early

win.text: They run into the fire. You kill two through it and the rush is dead.

lose.text: This time they waited for the fire to burn out. You are caught reloading.

choices.text: Give Banana, play a crossfire from Coffins and New Box

win.text: They pour onto the site and die between two angles.

lose.text: Two flashes, and neither of you sees the entry.

choices.text: Call a rotation from A before the round starts
choices.result: Three on B. They go A instead, onto a single defender.

events.text: {tournament}, Nuke. 1v1, the bomb is planted on the lower site. You are a CT at the top of Ramp with a kit and 25 seconds. You have no idea where the last T is.

choices.text: Fake the defuse, then swing the angle he must peek

win.text: He bites on the sound. You are already aiming at his head.

lose.text: He does not move. You run out of time on the real defuse.

choices.text: Smoke the bomb and stick the defuse

win.text: He sprays the smoke and misses everything. Defused.

lose.text: He sprays the smoke and does not miss.

events.text: {tournament}, Ancient, T side. Pistol round of the second half, 6-6. Your team wants a plan and looks at you.

choices.text: Five-man rush through B Ramp with two flashes

win.text: They were stacked A. You plant behind Pillar and win the round 5v2.

lose.text: Two CTs with armour were waiting at the top of the ramp.

choices.text: Take Mid control, then split A through Donut and A Main

win.text: The split arrives at the same second from both sides. Textbook.

lose.text: The Mid fight costs two players. The split never happens.

events.text: {tournament}, Anubis. 2v3, you are a T with the bomb in Canal. Your last teammate is at A Main with 40 HP. The CTs have just used their utility on B.

choices.text: Call him to fake A while you walk to B through Water

win.text: Two CTs rotate to A. You plant B alone and win the post-plant.

lose.text: Nobody rotates. Three rifles are waiting on B.

choices.text: Join him and hit A together, fast

win.text: He dies for the trade, you take two and plant in the open.

lose.text: The Heaven player shuts both of you down.

events.text: {tournament}, Cache, CT side. Last round of regulation, 11-12. You hold A alone from Quad. Footsteps: at least three in A Main, and a smoke lands on Highway.

choices.text: Fall back to Forklift, call the rotation and play for time

win.text: You stay alive for nine seconds. That is all your team needed.

lose.text: A flash over the site finds you in the open.

choices.text: Hold the Quad angle and take the first one out of Main

win.text: One, two, and the third backs off. Overtime.

lose.text: You get one. The trade is instant.

events.text: {tournament}. You lost the pistol round and the next one. The team has $2,400 each: enough for a risky force-buy, or nothing.

choices.text: Force: armour, Deagles, one flash each

win.text: Three Deagle headshots. Their economy is the broken one now.

lose.text: Lost. Now you have to eco twice.

choices.text: Full eco, stack one site and pray

win.text: They walk into the stack. Two rifles picked up for free.

lose.text: They go to the other site. At least the money is safe.

events.text: {tournament}. You were up 10-5, it is now 10-10. Nobody is talking. There is one tactical timeout left.

choices.text: Call the timeout and speak first

win.text: "Forget the score. Next round, default, play your spots." It lands.

lose.text: Your voice shakes. The silence comes back worse.

choices.text: Say nothing and win your own duels

win.text: A triple kill restarts the whole team.

lose.text: You overpeek, alone.

events.text: {tournament}, Mirage, CT side. You hold Window with the AWP. Their AWPer has peeked Top Mid at the same second two rounds in a row.

choices.text: Pre-aim his timing and take the duel

win.text: One shot. The casters replay it three times.

lose.text: He was a frame faster.

choices.text: Leave Window and surprise him from Short

win.text: He scopes an empty Window. You do not miss the side of his head.

lose.text: They take Mid for free and split B.

events.text: {tournament}, Dust II, CT side. Their AWPer has killed your Mid player through Mid Doors two rounds in a row, at the very first second.

choices.text: Smoke Mid Doors from spawn and cross behind it

win.text: The smoke lands on the pixel. He shoots at nothing and you own Mid.

lose.text: The smoke is a metre short. He takes the shot through the gap.

choices.text: Take the duel yourself, jumping across

win.text: A mid-air shot through the doors. Their AWP is on the floor before the round has started.

lose.text: Three rounds in a row now.

events.text: {tournament}, Dust II. You are the last player on the B site, on Platform, when four of them pour out of B Tunnels behind two flashes.

choices.text: Turn away from the flashes, then spray the tunnel exit

win.text: Three kills in one spray. The fourth plants alone and your rotation finishes him.

lose.text: You turn back half a second too early. White screen.

choices.text: Drop through Window and play the retake with your team

win.text: You stay alive, call four on B, and the 5v4 retake is clean.

lose.text: The retake comes through Mid Doors one by one.

events.text: {tournament}, Mirage, T side. Your team has lost three rounds hitting A. Your IGL asks for one piece of information before he calls: is anyone holding Apartments?

choices.text: Walk up silently and listen

win.text: One footstep on the Van. "Solo B, he is on Van." The execute takes eight seconds.

lose.text: He was waiting for you in silence too. He was better at it.

choices.text: Flash yourself through the window and take the space

win.text: Pop flash, one kill at Bench, and Market is yours.

lose.text: Two of them were stacked there. You trade one.

events.text: {tournament}, Mirage. 2v2 after the plant on A. You are in Palace, your teammate is at Ticket with 20 HP. The defuse sound starts.

choices.text: Wait. It is a fake

win.text: It stops after a second. He peeks Palace and finds you already aiming.

lose.text: It was not a fake. He had a kit and a smoke.

choices.text: Jump out and spray the bomb

win.text: You catch him on the bomb. Your teammate trades the last one from Ticket.

lose.text: The second CT was watching Palace from Jungle the whole time.

events.text: {tournament}, Inferno, T side. You are alone in Apartments while your team fakes Banana. The A site is quiet. Too quiet, or really empty?

choices.text: Wait for the rotation sound, then walk out

win.text: You hear them run through Arch. You plant for Pit and call your team back.

lose.text: Nobody rotated. The Pit player lets you walk out, then shoots you in the back.

choices.text: Go now, fast, and check Pit first

win.text: He is in Pit. You are faster. The site is open.

lose.text: He was in Library, not in Pit.

events.text: {tournament}, Inferno. 3v3 retake on B, bomb planted behind Coffins. You come from CT with a molotov. One of them is somewhere near New Box.

choices.text: Molotov New Box and take the site together

win.text: He has to leave the fire and runs into two rifles.

lose.text: The molotov bounces off the box and burns your own teammate.

choices.text: Keep the molotov for the bomb, to block the last second
choices.result: Not pretty, but the planter cannot hold his angle through the flames.

events.text: {tournament}, Nuke, T side. The plan is to cross Outside towards Secret. The wall of smokes is one smoke short: there is a gap, and an AWP is probably looking at it.

choices.text: Cross anyway, jumping, one by one

win.text: He misses the first, hesitates on the second. Four of you are in Secret.

lose.text: He does not miss the first.

choices.text: Cancel and hit Ramp instead, late

win.text: Their rotation is already Outside. Ramp is held by one player with a pistol.

lose.text: Twenty seconds is not enough to take Ramp.

events.text: {tournament}, Nuke, CT side. You hold the A site from Heaven. A noise in Vents, a flash over Hut, and footsteps in Lobby, all in the same second.

choices.text: Hold your position and call exactly what you hear

win.text: "One vents, four Hut, I hold Heaven." Your team is exactly where it should be.

lose.text: You call five A. Four of them were going down.

choices.text: Drop down and fight Hut before they are ready

win.text: Two kills through the door of Hut. The execute never starts.

lose.text: You fall into four crosshairs.

events.text: {tournament}, Ancient, CT side. You hold B alone from Pillar. A smoke blooms at the top of B Ramp and you hear someone drop into Cave.

choices.text: Spam through the smoke, then fall back

win.text: One kill through the smoke, 70 damage on another. They hesitate for ten precious seconds.

lose.text: The Cave player was already behind you.

choices.text: Leave the site and play the retake from Lane
choices.result: You give them the plant and keep five players. The retake is a coin flip you chose.

events.text: {tournament}, Ancient. 1v1, you are a CT in Temple, the bomb is down in A Main with the last T. Fifteen seconds. He has to come to you, or you have to go to him?

choices.text: Stay. The clock is on your side

win.text: He runs out with five seconds left, straight into your crosshair.

lose.text: He flashes over the wall. You never see him plant.

choices.text: Push through Donut and surprise him

win.text: He is looking at the site. You are behind him.

lose.text: He was waiting for exactly that.

events.text: {tournament}, Anubis, T side. You have taken Mid for free three rounds in a row. This round, the silence at Connector feels different.

choices.text: Throw a molotov deep before stepping in

win.text: Two CTs jump out of the fire. Their trap becomes your two free kills.

lose.text: Nobody was there. You hit a site without your molotov.

choices.text: Trust the habit and walk in

win.text: They are there, and you are faster.

lose.text: Two shotguns at point-blank range.

events.text: {tournament}, Anubis. Post-plant on A, 2v2. You are in Heaven with the AK of a dead teammate and twelve bullets. One CT is at Camera, the other is unknown.

choices.text: Let them come to the bomb and shoot the defuser

win.text: Six bullets for the defuser, six for his friend. Empty magazine, full arena.

lose.text: They smoke the bomb. Twelve bullets into grey.

choices.text: Peek Camera now, while it is a 1v1

win.text: One tap. The last CT saves his rifle.

lose.text: The unknown one was right under you.

events.text: {tournament}, Cache, T side. The round is slow. You are at Mid and you notice the CT at Z Connector has been throwing his smoke at the same second every round.

choices.text: Run through the smoke the moment it lands

win.text: He is still putting his rifle back in his hands. You are in their spawn with the whole map open.

lose.text: This round, his teammate was waiting behind it.

choices.text: Tell your IGL and let him use it later
choices.result: He keeps it for the round at 10-10. It works.

events.text: {tournament}, Cache. Match point for them. They run through B Main with the bomb, and you are in Sunroom with one flash. Your B partner is already dead in Checkers.

choices.text: Flash out of Sunroom and take them from the side

win.text: Three blind players on the site and one rifle on their flank. You save the match.

lose.text: The flash bounces back into the room. You blind yourself.

choices.text: Hide, let them plant, wait for your team

win.text: They never check Sunroom. When the retake starts, you are behind all of them.

lose.text: They check Sunroom.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. Pistol round. $800: armour and nothing else, or a better pistol and utility with no armour?

choices.text: Armour, and fight at close range

win.text: You tank two body shots at {spot} and win both duels.

lose.text: One headshot. Armour does not help against those.

choices.text: Utility for the team: a smoke and two flashes

win.text: Your flashes win the round for the four players with armour.

lose.text: Good flashes, lost duels. It happens.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. The round is lost: 1v3, bomb planted. You have an AWP worth $4,750 and a healthy bank. Three hunters are spreading out to find you.

choices.text: Save the AWP in the furthest corner of the map

win.text: They do not find you. Next round, your AWP wins the opening duel.

lose.text: They find you at {spot}. They leave with your AWP.

choices.text: Hunt one of the hunters for an exit kill

win.text: Two exit kills. Their economy takes the hit and yours survives.

lose.text: You lose the AWP and the duel. Your IGL sighs into the microphone.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. Overtime, 15-15. Your legs are shaking under the desk and your mouse feels heavier than in the first round.

choices.text: Slow everything down: one breath before every peek

win.text: Your hands stop shaking. You win the two duels that decide it.

lose.text: You breathe, you peek, you miss.

choices.text: Ride the adrenaline and play faster than them

win.text: They are tired too, and you are quicker. Four rounds in a row.

lose.text: Fast and wrong.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. Your star has missed three easy shots and has stopped talking. He is one bad round away from disappearing from the match.

choices.text: Give him your position and an easy round
choices.result: Two free kills at {spot} and he is back. You saw nothing of that round, and it was the most important one you played.

choices.text: A joke on comms to break the tension

win.text: He laughs despite himself. Next round, a triple kill.

lose.text: Wrong moment. He mutes the channel for a round.

choices.text: "Wake up."
choices.result: He wakes up angry, at you.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. Across the server: {rv}. He has taken the same duel against you at {spot} three times, and won two. He will come a fourth time.

choices.text: Change your angle by one metre and wait

win.text: He pre-fires the old angle. You are not there. He is dead.

lose.text: He guessed the new angle too. He knows you too well.

choices.text: Same angle, same duel. This is personal

win.text: 2-2. The caster says both your names in the same breath.

lose.text: 3-1 for him. He types nothing. That is worse.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}, T side, 9-9. They have rotated early on your last three executes. Thirty seconds on the clock and your team is set up for the same site again.

choices.text: Throw the full execute as a fake, then go the other way

win.text: Four CTs arrive on an empty site. You plant on the other one, walking.

lose.text: This time they did not rotate. And you have no utility left.

choices.text: Same execute, two seconds faster

win.text: The rotation arrives to find the bomb already down.

lose.text: Two seconds faster means two flashes too early.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. Your entry fragger is ready at {spot} and asks for a flash. You have one left, and you were keeping it for the retake.

choices.text: Throw it now, the way you practised

win.text: It pops above their heads. He takes two before they can see the floor.

lose.text: It pops in his face. He says nothing. You know.

choices.text: Keep it and go in with him as a second rifle

win.text: He dies, you trade, and you still have the flash for the retake.

lose.text: He dies without the flash he asked for.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. You are first through {spot}, as always. In the corner of your eye: a shadow that should not be there.

choices.text: Flick to the shadow

win.text: A close-range hider, dead before he fires. The site opens like a door.

lose.text: It was a decoy position. The real one was on the other side.

choices.text: Call it and keep running to make space

win.text: You die, but your call gives the trade and the site. That is the job.

lose.text: You die mid-sentence.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. You have been alone near {spot} for a minute. Your team is about to hit the other site. Go now, and you are early. Wait, and you may be late.

choices.text: Wait for the first shot, then move

win.text: The rotation runs past you, backs turned. Two kills they never see coming.

lose.text: The rotation went the other way. You arrive at a finished round.

choices.text: Go now and take their attention

win.text: One kill, two CTs turning towards you, and your team hits a half-empty site.

lose.text: You die alone, far from everyone, with no trade.

events.text: {tournament}, {map}. You missed the opening shot at {spot} and they know where you are. Your rifler shouts for you to fall back.

choices.text: Fall back, reposition, hold a new angle

win.text: They push the old spot. You are ten metres away with a loaded AWP.

lose.text: They flash you on the way out.

choices.text: Re-peek the same angle. He will not expect it

win.text: He expected nothing. One shot, and the confidence of a whole map.

lose.text: He expected it. Their AWPer now holds your AWP.

events.text: {tournament}, Dust II, CT side. You hold Long A from Car. Two flashes fly over the corner and you hear four pairs of feet running through the doors.

choices.text: Fall back to the site and hold the cross from Goose

win.text: They cross one by one into your crosshair. Two down before Short arrives.

lose.text: A smoke lands on the cross. You see nothing until they are on you.

choices.text: Stay at Car and fight blind

win.text: You spray the corner by ear. Three kills you never saw.

lose.text: White screen, then grey screen.

events.text: {tournament}, Dust II, T side. Your team has Catwalk. One smoke left, forty seconds, and the CTs have not shown a single player on A.

choices.text: Split: two up Short, three through Long

win.text: Both groups arrive together. The lone A player cannot look both ways.

lose.text: Long arrives five seconds late. Short dies alone.

choices.text: Drop to Mid and hit B through Mid Doors

win.text: They were stacked A. You plant B against one player.

lose.text: The Window player was waiting for exactly that sound.

events.text: {tournament}, Mirage, CT side. You anchor B alone from Van. No utility has been thrown at A for fifteen seconds, and the Apartments are too silent.

choices.text: Molotov the Apartments exit now and call for help

win.text: Five players stuck behind the fire for seven seconds. Your rotation arrives through Market just in time.

lose.text: Nobody was there. They hit A with your teammate out of position.

choices.text: Hide behind Bench and let them come

win.text: They run past you. Three kills in the back before anyone turns.

lose.text: The second player checks Bench. It is his job.

events.text: {tournament}, Mirage, T side. You control Mid with a teammate. Connector is smoked, Window is not. Your IGL waits for your call: A through Connector, or B through Short?

choices.text: B through Short, fast, before they read it

win.text: The Short player is looking at the smoke. You are already past him.

lose.text: The Window AWP was not smoked for a reason.

choices.text: Wait in Connector smoke and pinch A with the team

win.text: You step out of the smoke as the execute lands. Jungle and Stairs fall together.

lose.text: A CT pushes through the smoke into you.

events.text: {tournament}, Inferno, CT side. You play Pit on A. They have Apartments and Second Mid, and a smoke lands exactly on your angle.

choices.text: Leave Pit through the smoke and play from Graveyard

win.text: They clear an empty Pit with three grenades. You shoot from where nobody looks.

lose.text: A molotov on Graveyard. They had done their homework.

choices.text: Stay in Pit, crouched, and wait for the first legs

win.text: Legs, then heads. Two kills from a place they thought was gone.

lose.text: The grenade arrives before the legs.

events.text: {tournament}, Inferno, T side. You are the Boiler player on an A execute. The flashes are in the air. Go first, or let your entry go first?

choices.text: Go first and clear Library

win.text: Library is blind. One tap and the site is cut in half.

lose.text: He turned away from the flash. He was not blind at all.

choices.text: Trade behind your entry

win.text: He dies, you trade in half a second. That is how sites are taken.

lose.text: You are a step too far behind. No trade.

events.text: {tournament}, Nuke. The bomb is planted on the lower site and you are the last CT, upstairs, with 28 seconds. Vents is the fast way down. It is also the loud way.

choices.text: Vents, and shoot the moment you land

win.text: He is looking at the door. You drop behind him. Defuse with two seconds left.

lose.text: He heard the vent break and aimed at the exit.

choices.text: Take the long way round through Ramp, silently

win.text: You arrive with eight seconds and a kit. He never heard a thing.

lose.text: Silent, and one second too late.

events.text: {tournament}, Nuke, T side. Three rounds in a row, a CT has pushed Lobby through Squeaky and killed one of you. Your team wants revenge.

choices.text: Set a trap: you wait behind the door with a shotgun

win.text: The door opens. One shot. He does not push Lobby again that half.

lose.text: This round, of course, he stays home. You have a shotgun and nowhere to use it.

choices.text: Ignore him and rush Outside while he is away from his post

win.text: Their defence has a hole exactly where he should have been.

lose.text: He hears the rush and comes back through Garage behind you.

events.text: {tournament}, Ancient, CT side. You fight for Mid every round and you win it every round. This time the T side sends three players there.

choices.text: Fall back towards Red Room and call it

win.text: "Three Mid, they are going Elbow." Your B players turn and the round is read.

lose.text: They went Donut. Your call sends everyone the wrong way.

choices.text: Hold the angle. You have won it five times

win.text: Six times. Then seven, then eight. A triple kill at Mid.

lose.text: Three rifles against one is arithmetic.

events.text: {tournament}, Ancient, T side. You are in A Main with the bomb and one teammate. The other three are dead at B. Twenty-five seconds.

choices.text: Smoke Temple and plant in the open

win.text: The plant goes down. Your teammate holds Donut and the CTs run out of time.

lose.text: Someone was already on the site, behind the boxes.

choices.text: Save both rifles
choices.result: Two AKs for the next round. Nobody in the arena applauds a save.

events.text: {tournament}, Anubis, CT side. You hold B from Pillar. A smoke lands at the B Main entrance and you hear one, only one, set of footsteps in Water.

choices.text: It is a fake. Tell A to stay

win.text: Ten seconds later, four of them hit A into a full defence. Your call won the round.

lose.text: It was not a fake. The other four were walking.

choices.text: Push through the smoke and kill the lone player

win.text: He is alone, with the bomb. You kill him and stand on it.

lose.text: He was the bait.

events.text: {tournament}, Anubis, T side. Your default has found nothing after a minute. You are near Palace with a flash and a decision to make.

choices.text: Flash and take the space alone to open the round

win.text: One kill, one retreat, and the map opens. Your IGL calls the site in two words.

lose.text: Two players were waiting. 4v5 with thirty seconds.

choices.text: Wait and regroup for a five-man hit

win.text: Five players, four grenades, one site. Nothing clever, everything on time.

lose.text: The regroup takes too long. You plant with three seconds and no positions.

events.text: {tournament}, Cache, T side. Your team is stacked in A Main. The first man out has died three rounds in a row to a player hidden at Forklift.

choices.text: Molotov Forklift before anyone steps out

win.text: He runs out of the flames into five crosshairs.

lose.text: The molotov hits the fork and burns nothing.

choices.text: Go first yourself and pre-aim the spot

win.text: Your crosshair is already on his head when you turn the corner.

lose.text: This round he is in Quad instead.

events.text: {tournament}, Cache, CT side. You rotate from B to A through Highway, alone, when a flash pops in front of you and the bomb sound says "A".

choices.text: Wait for your second rotation before peeking

win.text: Two angles at the same second. The retake takes six seconds.

lose.text: The bomb is planted in the safest spot on the site while you wait.

choices.text: Peek now to stop the plant

win.text: You kill the planter with the bomb at 90 %.

lose.text: Three players were watching Highway.

events.text: The coach introduces a new rule: every lost scrim is reviewed in full the same evening, however late it is. The first review ends at 1 a.m.

choices.text: Back the rule in front of the team
choices.result: The scrims become very serious, very fast. Nobody wants a 1 a.m. review.

choices.text: Propose a limit: forty-five minutes, the five worst rounds

win.text: The coach agrees. The team owes you forty hours of sleep this year.

lose.text: "The five worst rounds are all of them." Tonight's review is longer.

events.text: The team hires a nutritionist. The energy drinks disappear from the practice room. So do the crisps. There is a bowl of almonds.

choices.text: Follow the plan for a month
choices.result: The third map of a series no longer feels like the fifth.

choices.text: Start a secret snack drawer for the whole team
choices.result: The nutritionist finds it in a week. He takes a chocolate bar and says nothing.

events.text: End-of-year team dinner, with a gift exchange. You have drawn your IGL's name. Budget: twenty dollars.

choices.text: A notebook titled "Strats that work (empty)"

win.text: He laughs until he cries and uses it for the whole next season.

lose.text: You lost a final last week on his call. Bad timing.

choices.text: A framed photo of the team's best moment of the year
choices.result: It ends up on the wall of the practice room.

events.text: A strat you invented last week is used against you in an official match, grenade for grenade. Someone talked, or someone watched a scrim they should not have.

choices.text: Propose stricter rules: no streaming scrims, no sharing demos
choices.result: Nobody is accused. The leak stops.

choices.text: Ask out loud who has friends in that team
choices.result: Everyone has friends in every team. Now everyone is a suspect.

choices.text: Turn it around: build a counter to your own strat

win.text: Next time they copy you, they walk into a trap built for them.

lose.text: A week of work on a counter nobody ever needs.

events.text: The club brings in a sports psychologist for group sessions. First exercise: say one thing you appreciate about the teammate on your left, out loud.

choices.text: Take it seriously
choices.result: It is awkward for exactly one minute. Then someone says something true, and the room changes.

choices.text: "He has a very nice mousepad."
choices.result: Laughter. The psychologist writes something down.

events.text: A salary figure leaks in the team group chat by mistake. The newest player earns more than you, and everyone saw it before the message was deleted.

choices.text: Raise it with management, privately, with {agent}

win.text: {agent} gets you a quiet adjustment. Nobody in the team ever knows.

lose.text: "The market changed." Nothing else changes.

choices.text: Let it go. He did not write his own contract
choices.result: He is visibly relieved when you sit next to him at lunch.

choices.text: Make a joke of it for a week: "Ask the rich one."
choices.result: Funny on Monday. Less funny on Friday.

events.text: You have just come back from 2-12 to win 16-14. Nobody can sleep. It is 1 a.m. in the hotel corridor and five adults are re-enacting rounds with their hands.

choices.text: Stay up with them. Nights like this are rare
choices.result: Tomorrow's match will be played tired and fearless.

choices.text: Send everyone to bed. The tournament is not over
choices.result: Groans, then doors closing. Someone thanks you at breakfast.

events.text: Two days before an event abroad, a teammate's visa is refused. The team can play with the coach as fifth player, or withdraw.

choices.text: Play. Take two roles yourself to cover the gap

win.text: You win a map nobody thought you could. The coach gets one kill and frames the screenshot.

lose.text: Out in two maps, but the absent teammate watched every round and will not forget it.

choices.text: Vote to withdraw and prepare the next event properly
choices.result: A sensible decision that feels like nothing.

events.text: {journalist} publishes it before anyone has called you: "{rival} are interested in {name}." Your teammates read it at breakfast.

choices.text: Tell the team first: "I know nothing, and I am here."
choices.result: The rumour dies in the practice room, where it matters.

choices.text: Say nothing and let your value go up
choices.result: Management offers a small raise to "clarify things". The room is cooler.

choices.text: Ask {agent} to find out if it is real
choices.result: "Half real. They asked about your price, then about three other players."

events.text: For a month the coach wants to try something: you play a different role in scrims, "to understand what the others need from you".

choices.text: Commit to it fully
choices.result: You are bad at it. You also finally understand why your flash requests annoyed everyone.

choices.text: Do it, but keep an hour a day on your real role
choices.result: You lose nothing and learn a little.

events.text: A message from someone called {agent}: "I represent players. You are underpaid and you do not know it. Ten per cent, and I handle everything."

choices.text: Sign with {agent}
choices.result: Your next contract has four pages you would never have read. {agent} read them.

choices.text: Handle your own business
choices.result: "The offer stays open," writes {agent}. It does.

events.text: Your online stats are excellent. On LAN, in front of people, your numbers drop every time. {journalist} writes the word everyone avoids: "onliner".

choices.text: Practise at the club with noise in your headset and people behind you
choices.result: The staff takes turns shouting behind your chair. It is ridiculous and it works.

choices.text: Prove it at the next LAN

win.text: MVP of the event. The article gets a follow-up with a different word.

lose.text: You think about the word during every duel.

events.text: The draw puts you against the team that let you go years ago. Their manager, the one who said you were "not ready", is in the front row.

choices.text: Play your normal game
choices.result: You win, shake every hand, his included. That is the whole revenge.

choices.text: Make it a statement game

win.text: Thirty-five kills. You look at the front row once. Only once.

lose.text: You force everything. He does not even need to smile.

events.text: The club wants one player at every sponsor event this season: dinners, store openings, a television show. They ask for volunteers and everyone looks at their shoes.

choices.text: Volunteer
choices.result: Your teammates owe you a lot of free evenings. Sponsors now ask for you by name.

choices.text: Propose a rotation: one event each
choices.result: Fair. Your AWPer gets the television show and is surprisingly good at it.

events.text: The team asks everyone to move to the city where the practice facility is. For you, it means another country, another language, and your friends on video calls.

choices.text: Move, and take language lessons
choices.result: The first winter is long. By spring you order food without pointing.

choices.text: Negotiate: two weeks there, two weeks at home
choices.result: You live in airports, but you live near your people.

events.text: Your sleep tracker shows the truth: five hours a night for a month, and a reaction time that gets worse every week.

choices.text: Screens off at midnight, no exceptions
choices.result: Your late-night viewers complain. Your first duel of the morning does not.

choices.text: Coffee exists for a reason
choices.result: It works until the afternoon. Every afternoon.

events.text: Your oldest friend, the one you played your first games with in an internet café, is in town for one evening. You have an important scrim block at the same time.

choices.text: Ask the coach for the evening off
choices.result: Four hours of old stories. He still calls you by your very first nickname.

choices.text: Invite him to watch the scrims from behind your chair
choices.result: You play like someone is watching, because someone is. Dinner at midnight.

events.text: With real money in your account for the first time, the proposals arrive: a friend's clothing brand, a share in an internet café, or a boring savings plan from the bank.

choices.text: The boring savings plan
choices.result: Nothing to post about. Something to retire on.

choices.text: The internet café, in your home town

win.text: Full every weekend. There is a framed jersey of yours above the counter.

lose.text: It closes after a year. The kids who trained there still thank you.

choices.text: The clothing brand, with your name on it

win.text: The first drop sells out in a day.

lose.text: You own four hundred hoodies in size XL.

events.text: A patch changes the price of the AWP and of armour. Overnight, every team's economy plan is out of date, including yours.

choices.text: Do the maths tonight and propose new buy rules
choices.result: A spreadsheet with three colours. Your team is the first to adapt.

choices.text: Play and feel it out
choices.result: You lose two rounds to a broken economy before the habit forms.

events.text: A map returns to the competitive pool after years away. Half the scene has never played it at pro level. Your coach asks who wants to own it.

choices.text: Take it: fifty hours alone on an empty server
choices.result: You find a smoke nobody uses yet. For three months, it is your team's secret.

choices.text: Watch how the best teams play it first
choices.result: You copy the meta instead of making it. Safe.

events.text: Review session. The numbers are clear: your team loses one anti-eco round in four. Rounds you should win with your eyes closed.

choices.text: Propose a rule: nobody peeks alone against pistols
choices.result: Boring rounds. Won rounds.

choices.text: Admit that the one who peeks alone is usually you
choices.result: Saying it first makes the rest of the meeting very short.

events.text: Your coach wants you to give up your favourite CT position so the team can fix a weak spot.

choices.text: Accept and learn the new spot seriously

win.text: Two weeks later you hold it better than the player you replaced.

lose.text: You look lost for a month. The team still appreciates the effort.

choices.text: Refuse. That spot is where you win rounds
choices.result: You keep the position. The coach keeps the note.

events.text: {team} offers to extend your contract. The number on the page is the same as last year.

choices.text: Ask for a real raise, with your stats on the table

win.text: They fold faster than expected.

lose.text: "We will talk again after the next event." The room is cold.

choices.text: Sign as it is. You are here to win
choices.result: Management notes your attitude.

choices.text: Hire an agent to handle it
choices.result: He takes his cut, you take the rest and stop thinking about it.

events.text: Two weeks of bootcamp before the next event: twelve hours a day in the same room, same hotel, same five faces.

choices.text: All in. First to arrive, last to leave
choices.result: The team has never looked this sharp. You are exhausted.

choices.text: Do the work, protect your sleep
choices.result: Steady progress. You arrive at the event fresh.

choices.text: Ask for a lighter schedule
choices.result: You get it. Two teammates raise an eyebrow.

events.text: Three bad results in a row. In the practice room nobody speaks, and management "wants to review the roster".

choices.text: Call a team talk and say what nobody says

win.text: An hour of honesty. The next scrim feels like a different team.

lose.text: It turns into a blame game. You started it.

choices.text: Shut up and fix your own game
choices.result: Your numbers go up. The silence stays.

choices.text: Tell management you are not the problem
choices.result: It leaks to the team within a day.

events.text: A 17-year-old from the academy joins practice. He is fast, loud and makes the same mistakes you made at his age.

choices.text: Take him under your wing
choices.result: Teaching the game makes you understand it better.

choices.text: Let him figure it out. Nobody helped you
choices.result: He figures it out. Slowly.

events.text: You just lost a series you should have won. A microphone appears: "What went wrong today?"

choices.text: "I missed shots I have to hit. That one is on me."
choices.result: The clip gets shared with one word: "Professional."

choices.text: "The veto was lost before we sat down."
choices.result: Your coach reads the interview on the bus.

choices.text: Short answers, walk away
choices.result: Nothing to quote. Nothing to regret.

events.text: {rival} offers a week of scrims. Their star, {star}, is in the form of his life.

choices.text: Play your real strats and learn from the beating
choices.result: You lose most maps and learn more than in a month of wins.

choices.text: Hide everything, play defaults
choices.result: Nobody shows anything. It is basically a deathmatch with smokes.

events.text: 9-12 down. In the timeout, a teammate cuts you off: "Your calls are not working. Let us just play loose."

choices.text: Hold your ground and call the round you prepared

win.text: The call works. So does the next one. Nobody questions you again.

lose.text: The round fails. You can hear what they are thinking.

choices.text: Let them play loose for a half
choices.result: It half works. Your authority takes the hit.

events.text: The economy is broken after two lost force-buys. There is money for rifles for everyone, or for your AWP and two pistols.

choices.text: Insist on the AWP. That is your job

win.text: Opening pick, then a second one. The gamble pays.

lose.text: You miss the first shot and the AWP ends up in enemy hands.

choices.text: Take a rifle so everyone can buy
choices.result: A full buy wins the round. The AWP can wait.

events.text: You have died first in four T rounds in a row, without a trade. A teammate offers to take the entry for the rest of the half.

choices.text: Keep the entry and ask for a flash this time

win.text: The flash pops, you take two. The site opens.

lose.text: Dead first again.

choices.text: Swap and play the trade behind him
choices.result: From second position you finally see why it was not working.

events.text: Your IGL wants you closer to the pack: "We need a fifth gun on executes, not a ghost on the other side of the map."

choices.text: Show him your timings on the demo

win.text: "Fine. Keep the lurk, but call earlier." You both win.

lose.text: The demo shows three rounds where you arrived ten seconds late.

choices.text: Play with the pack for now
choices.result: The executes are cleaner. You miss the flanks.

events.text: After a big win, every highlight is about your star player. Nobody mentions the four flashes that set him up.

choices.text: That is the job. Keep feeding him
choices.result: In the team house, everyone knows who wins those rounds.

choices.text: Ask for a few rounds built around you

win.text: You get them, and you deliver. Your rating jumps.

lose.text: The rounds go badly. The request is remembered.

events.text: Fans keep asking when you will stream. You have two free evenings a week.

choices.text: Stream both evenings
choices.result: The channel grows fast. Your sleep does not.

choices.text: One relaxed stream a week
choices.result: A small, loyal chat.

choices.text: No stream. Evenings are for recovery
choices.result: You are the freshest player at practice.

events.text: After a bad game, an account with 200k followers posts your worst round with the caption "Paid actor?".

choices.text: Ignore it. Phone face down
choices.result: By tomorrow they have a new target.

choices.text: Reply with a joke at your own expense

win.text: Your reply gets more likes than the post.

lose.text: It reads as salty. Screenshots everywhere.

choices.text: Fire back in the replies
choices.result: It becomes the story of the week. Your team's manager calls.

events.text: Fourteen hours of flight, seven time zones, first match in 36 hours.

choices.text: Follow the sleep plan from the team's performance coach
choices.result: Boring, effective.

choices.text: Cannot sleep anyway: deathmatch until sunrise
choices.result: Your aim is warm. Your brain is not.

events.text: The team hires a physical trainer. First session is at 8 a.m., optional.

choices.text: Go, and keep going
choices.result: By the third week, long best-of-threes stop feeling long.

choices.text: Optional means optional
choices.result: You sleep in.

events.text: Your sister's wedding is on the same weekend as an online qualifier. The team can play with a stand-in.

choices.text: Go to the wedding
choices.result: The team scrapes through without you. You do not regret it.

choices.text: Play the qualifier
choices.result: You qualify. The family group chat is very quiet.

events.text: A peripherals brand offers you a personal deal: your name on a mouse, four content days a year.

choices.text: Sign it
choices.result: The mouse sells. The shooting days are long.

choices.text: Negotiate: more money, fewer days

win.text: Double the fee, two days. Done.

lose.text: They sign someone else.

choices.text: Decline. No distractions
choices.result: Your schedule stays empty. So does your inbox.

events.text: For the first time, you launch the game and feel nothing. The season is only half done.

choices.text: Tell the coach and take a week off
choices.result: A week of nothing. The itch comes back.

choices.text: Push through. Everyone is tired

win.text: You find a second wind.

lose.text: Your form collapses for a month.

events.text: A dull pain in your wrist after every long session. It has been three weeks.

choices.text: See a physiotherapist and follow the exercises
choices.result: Ten minutes of stretching a day. The pain fades.

choices.text: Play through it

win.text: It goes away on its own. This time.

lose.text: It gets worse. Two weeks without touching a mouse.

events.text: Someone digs up a voice clip of you at 16, raging at a teammate in a FACEIT game. It is spreading.

choices.text: Short apology: "I was a kid. I am not proud of it."
choices.result: The story dies in a day.

choices.text: Say nothing
choices.result: It lingers for a week, then fades.

choices.text: Turn it into a joke

win.text: It becomes a meme, and you own it.

lose.text: People read it as not taking it seriously.

events.text: A CS2 update lands the week before an event: smoke timings change and half of your team's lineups no longer work.

choices.text: Spend two nights on an empty server relearning everything
choices.result: You post the new lineups in the team chat before breakfast.

choices.text: Wait for the coach to send the fixes
choices.result: They arrive the day before the match.

events.text: Valve rotates the map pool. Your team's best map is gone, and nobody has ever played the new one seriously.

choices.text: Volunteer to learn it first and brief the team
choices.result: For a month, you are the team's expert on it.

choices.text: Ban it in every veto and hope
choices.result: It works until somebody notices.

events.text: A new coach arrives with a strict system: fixed roles, fixed positions, a written playbook.

choices.text: Buy in completely
choices.result: The team finally looks like one team.

choices.text: Challenge the parts that hurt your game

win.text: He adapts two setups for you. Respect earned.

lose.text: "My system or the bench."

events.text: Team meeting about identity: play fast and take map control early, or slow defaults and late executes?

choices.text: Vote fast: duels, trades, pressure
choices.result: The team plays on instinct.

choices.text: Vote slow: information, utility, structure
choices.result: Fewer highlights, more rounds.

events.text: The analyst sends a 40-page document on {rival} the night before you play them.

choices.text: Read all of it
choices.result: You know their pistol rounds better than they do.

choices.text: Read your positions only, then sleep
choices.result: Enough to not be surprised.

events.text: Team dinner after a long scrim day. The bill arrives and everyone suddenly studies their phone.

choices.text: Pay for the table
choices.result: "Next one is on me." It never is, but nobody forgets tonight.

choices.text: Loser of a 1v1 on aim_map pays

win.text: You win the bracket on a laptop trackpad. Legend status in the group chat.

lose.text: You lose the final 16-14 and pay for five desserts.

choices.text: Split it to the cent
choices.result: Fair. A little cold.

events.text: A teammate arrives forty minutes late to practice for the third time this month. The coach says nothing. The room waits for someone to.

choices.text: Talk to him alone after practice

win.text: There was a reason, and it was not laziness. He is on time from now on.

lose.text: "Who made you captain?" The conversation ends there.

choices.text: Call him out in front of everyone
choices.result: He is on time the next day, and does not speak to you for a week.

choices.text: Not your problem
choices.result: Nobody says anything. The habit spreads.

events.text: Hotel rooms are shared at this event. Your roommate plays deathmatch until 3 a.m. with his keyboard on the desk next to your pillow.

choices.text: Agree on a curfew, like adults
choices.result: Midnight, headphones, lights off. Simple.

choices.text: Join him. Sleep is for the flight home
choices.result: Two hours of 1v1s and laughing. Tomorrow will be long.

choices.text: Ask the manager for a single room
choices.result: You sleep nine hours. He learns about it from the manager.

events.text: Lost round, mid-scrim. A teammate throws his hands up: "Where was the flash? Every time." He is looking at you.

choices.text: "My bad. Next round I call it earlier."
choices.result: The tension drops in one sentence.

choices.text: "Watch the demo. You peeked before my call."

win.text: The demo agrees with you. He nods, annoyed. Fair is fair.

lose.text: The demo shows your flash landing behind a wall.

choices.text: Explode. You have been carrying his rounds for weeks
choices.result: The scrim ends early. The coach wants to see you both tomorrow.

events.text: It is {mate}'s birthday in the middle of a bootcamp. The manager forgot. Practice starts in an hour.

choices.text: Run out, find a cake, hide it in the practice room
choices.result: Five players singing badly around a supermarket cake. A good day.

choices.text: Dedicate your first ace of the day to him

win.text: Third map, pistol round, five kills. "Happy birthday." The room loses it.

lose.text: No ace all day. You announce it anyway at dinner, as a debt.

events.text: A new player joins the roster. He is quiet, eats alone, and plays scrims as if he were afraid to make a call.

choices.text: Sit with him and ask about his old team
choices.result: By the end of the week he is the loudest voice in the trades.

choices.text: Let him settle in at his own pace
choices.result: It takes him two months.

choices.text: Test him: steal his position in a scrim to see how he reacts
choices.result: He says nothing. The others noticed.

events.text: Someone posts your worst whiff of the day in the team group chat, in slow motion, with circus music.

choices.text: Reply with an even worse clip of yourself
choices.result: It becomes a weekly tradition: the Friday fail.

choices.text: Dig up his worst round and post it with a full edit

win.text: The edit is so good the social media manager asks for the file.

lose.text: It was a round from the series you lost. Too soon.

choices.text: Leave the chat on read
choices.result: The joke dies. So does the mood.

events.text: Bus to the arena. One speaker, five opinions. Your IGL wants silence, your AWPer wants techno, and someone hands you the phone.

choices.text: Put on the cheesiest song you know and sing
choices.result: By the second chorus the whole bus is in. Nobody is nervous any more.

choices.text: Headphones for everyone, each his own
choices.result: A quiet bus, five different playlists.

events.text: Salaries are two weeks late. The manager says "it is being processed". In the practice room, the talk is no longer about strats.

choices.text: Speak for the team, calmly, with the manager

win.text: The money arrives in three days, with an apology. The team now looks at you differently.

lose.text: "Processing" for another month. At least you tried.

choices.text: Post about it publicly
choices.result: The money arrives the next morning. So does a very formal email.

choices.text: Keep your head down and keep practising
choices.result: You get paid eventually. Nobody played well in the meantime.

events.text: Role meeting. Two players want the same spot on the T side of {map}, the one that gets the opening duels and the highlights. You are one of them.

choices.text: Offer a trial: one week each, the stats decide

win.text: Your week is clearly better. He shakes your hand: "It is yours."

lose.text: His week is better. You take the support spot without a word.

choices.text: Give it to him. The team matters more
choices.result: He owes you one, and he knows it.

choices.text: Refuse to move. You are the better player
choices.result: You keep the spot and lose the room.

events.text: In the heat of a round, two teammates switch to their native language. You and the fourth player hear noise, not information.

choices.text: Propose ten fixed words everyone must use
choices.result: A laminated sheet above every monitor. It works.

choices.text: Learn their fifty most used words
choices.result: Your accent makes them cry laughing. Your calls land.

choices.text: Complain to the coach
choices.result: He raises it in the next meeting. The two of them know who talked.

events.text: One free day in a foreign city between two events. The team asks what you want to do.

choices.text: Go-karting. Loser carries the bags tomorrow
choices.result: Your IGL drives exactly the way he calls: slow, then all at once.

choices.text: Everyone rests. Meet at dinner
choices.result: A long nap and a long dinner.

choices.text: Extra practice. Free days are for other teams
choices.result: Sharp aim, heavy sighs.

events.text: A teammate is ill the morning of an online match. The stand-in is a kid from the academy, {rookie}, who has never played an official game.

choices.text: Give him the easy role and talk him through every round

win.text: {rookie} plays the game of his life. He will remember who made it easy.

lose.text: He freezes anyway. You lose, but he thanks you after.

choices.text: Play your own game and let him sink or swim
choices.result: He survives the map. Barely.

events.text: {rookie}, the academy kid you once helped through his first official match, is now a starter in a rival team. He sends you a message before you play each other.

choices.text: "Proud of you. I am still going to destroy you."
choices.result: He posts the screenshot. The community loves it.

choices.text: Give him one last piece of advice
choices.result: In his next interview he calls you the reason he made it.

events.text: The team is in a great mood. Someone suggests swapping the IGL's mouse sensitivity before the warm-up, "just to see".

choices.text: Do it, and film his face

win.text: He spins 720 degrees on his first peek and laughs harder than anyone.

lose.text: He does not find it funny today. At all.

choices.text: Not before an official match
choices.result: Someone calls you "dad" for the rest of the day.

events.text: The team has split in two: three who eat together and two who do not. You are invited to both tables, never at the same time.

choices.text: Book one big table and do not ask anyone's opinion

win.text: Awkward for ten minutes. Then someone tells the story of his worst LAN, and it is over.

lose.text: Two of them do not show up.

choices.text: Pick the bigger table
choices.result: Now it is four against one.

choices.text: Eat alone with a demo on your phone
choices.result: Three tables.

events.text: The manager asks to see you. "Your level is not the problem. The way you talk to people is. Two of your teammates came to me."

choices.text: Listen, and apologise to the team the same day
choices.result: It costs you more than a lost final. It changes the room.

choices.text: "I talk like someone who wants to win."
choices.result: "Then win. Because right now that is the only thing keeping your seat."

choices.text: Ask to work with the team's mental coach
choices.result: Six sessions. You learn to hear how you sound.

events.text: Half-time of an official match, 4-8 down. The room is flat. You feel the words coming, and they are not polite.

choices.text: Let it out: nobody here is playing like he wants it

win.text: Silence, then your IGL: "He is right." You win the second half 9-2.

lose.text: Two players stop talking for the rest of the match.

choices.text: Breathe. One calm sentence about the next round
choices.result: Nothing magical. The second half is tighter.

events.text: After two seasons, the team votes for a captain: the one who speaks to management and to the press. Three votes out of four have your name.

choices.text: Accept
choices.result: More meetings, more interviews, more weight. It suits you.

choices.text: Decline and nominate the fourth vote
choices.result: He never forgets it.

events.text: Eleven-hour flight home after going out in the first round. You are seated between your coach and the teammate who lost the deciding 1v1.

choices.text: Talk to the teammate about anything but the game
choices.result: Football, films, his dog. Somewhere over the ocean he says thanks.

choices.text: Review the demo with the coach, right now
choices.result: Useful. The teammate pretends to sleep.

choices.text: Headphones, hood, sleep
choices.result: You land rested. Nothing was said.

events.text: Before a scrim, a teammate proposes a bet: the bottom fragger changes his in-game name to "bot" for a week, on stream too.

choices.text: Accept, obviously

win.text: Your IGL is "bot" for seven days. Viewers love it.

lose.text: You are "bot" for seven days. Your chat will never let it go.

choices.text: Refuse. Scrims are for work
choices.result: "Okay, coach."

events.text: The coach gathers four of you, without the fifth. "Management wants to replace him. I want to know what you think before I answer."

choices.text: Defend him: he needs a different role, not the door

win.text: The role change works. He never learns how close it was. The coach does not forget who spoke.

lose.text: They replace him anyway, and the results do not improve.

choices.text: Say nothing either way
choices.result: He is gone within a week. You were in the room.

choices.text: Agree with management
choices.result: The new player is better. The old one unfollows all four of you.

events.text: You are {age}. The coach closes the door. "Your reflexes are not what they were at 22, and you know it. But nobody here reads the game like you. I want you to become our in-game leader. Less aim, more brain. Think about it."

choices.text: Accept. A second career starts today
choices.result: You hand over your position and pick up the notebook. The first weeks are rough: you call rounds half a second too late. But the team listens.

choices.text: Refuse. You are a fragger, and you will stay one
choices.result: "Your choice." He writes something down. From now on, every duel you lose will be counted.

events.text: Your first official match as in-game leader. 0-3 down after three rounds of your calls. In the timeout, four pairs of eyes turn to you.

choices.text: "My reads were wrong. New plan, here is why."

win.text: The adjustment works. You win the half 8-4, and something clicks: this is yours now.

lose.text: The new plan fails too. You will need time, and the team gives it to you.

choices.text: Let the old IGL call the rest of the map
choices.result: It stabilises the map and delays the question.

events.text: Pre-season. You have two weeks to decide how your team will play this year. The whiteboard is empty.

choices.text: A loose system: defaults, then let your stars read the round

win.text: Your fraggers feel trusted and it shows on the scoreboard.

lose.text: Without structure, the mid-rounds turn into five solo queues.

choices.text: A strict playbook: forty set plays, everyone learns all of them
choices.result: Boring to learn, hard to play against.

choices.text: Ask each player what he needs to be at his best
choices.result: Five conversations, five different answers. You build the system around them.

events.text: Your best fragger ignores your call for the third time in a map and takes a solo duel. He wins it. The round is still lost.

choices.text: Talk to him after the match: give him freedom, inside a frame

win.text: "Two rounds a half are yours. The rest, you are mine." He grins. Deal.

lose.text: He hears a leash. The next map is worse.

choices.text: Call him out on comms, right now
choices.result: He obeys for the rest of the map, and plays like a man in handcuffs.

choices.text: Build the next round around his solo play
choices.result: If you cannot stop the river, dig the canal.

events.text: The night before a playoff match against {rival}. Your analyst has found a pattern: they always fake A before a late B hit when the score is tied.

choices.text: Build a trap for that exact round and keep it secret until then

win.text: 11-11. They fake A. Four of yours are waiting on B. The casters call it mind reading.

lose.text: They changed the pattern this week. Your stack is on the wrong site.

choices.text: Share it with the team and adapt round by round
choices.result: No miracle round, but nobody is ever surprised.

events.text: You finish a won series with 9 kills in two maps. The comments are split between "genius caller" and "playing 4v5".

choices.text: Accept it. Your job is the other four's stats
choices.result: You stop opening the scoreboard after matches. You sleep better.

choices.text: Give yourself easier positions and one hour of aim a day
choices.result: Fifteen kills a map is enough to quiet the comments.

choices.text: Take the entry role next match to prove a point

win.text: Twenty-four kills and the calls. Nobody types "4v5" tonight.

lose.text: You die first and call from the grave. The round plan dies with you.

events.text: Deciding map, 10-12 down, last tactical timeout. You have thirty seconds and four exhausted players.

choices.text: One simple round, explained in ten seconds. Then silence

win.text: Simple works. Three rounds in a row, overtime, and the map.

lose.text: The round is simple. They read it simply.

choices.text: A round nobody has ever seen you play

win.text: A fake inside a fake. The other IGL takes his headset off and applauds.

lose.text: Two of your players go to the wrong site. Too clever, too late.

events.text: Management signs an 18-year-old prodigy and puts him in your hands. He out-aims everyone and has never held a site for a full round.

choices.text: Simplify his job: three rules, no more
choices.result: "Do not die first on CT. Trade or be traded. Tell me what you see." He blossoms.

choices.text: Spend your evenings reviewing his demos with him
choices.result: In six months he reads rounds like a veteran. You are tired and proud.

choices.text: Let him run free and cover his mistakes yourself
choices.result: He gets the highlights. You get the trades.

events.text: A young IGL from another team asks if he can pick your brain for an hour. He is your opponent next month.

choices.text: Tell him everything. The game needs good callers
choices.result: He beats you with one of your own ideas, and thanks you on stage.

choices.text: Help him, but keep your playbook closed
choices.result: Principles, not plays. He leaves with a full notebook anyway.

events.text: Opening duel, same angle you have held for ten years. An 18-year-old swings and you are dead before your finger moves. It is the fourth time this map.

choices.text: Stop taking the angle. Play off-angles and utility
choices.result: You survive longer. You are no longer the player who opens rounds.

choices.text: Take it again. You were faster than him at his age

win.text: One clean headshot. For one round you are 22 again.

lose.text: Five times. The coach looks at the screen, then at his notes.

events.text: The analyst shows the yearly numbers. Your opening duel success rate has dropped twelve points. The slide stays on the screen a little too long.

choices.text: Ask for a different role in the system
choices.result: You become the second man in, the one who trades. It is not what you signed up for at 16.

choices.text: "Numbers do not show impact."
choices.result: Nobody answers. That is an answer.

choices.text: Two extra hours of aim every morning before practice
choices.result: You slow the slide down. You do not stop it.

events.text: After a five-map day, your forearm needs twenty minutes of stretching before your fingers work properly again. The younger players are already queueing.

choices.text: Build a real routine: physio, sleep, shorter sessions
choices.result: Less volume, more quality. It buys you time.

choices.text: Keep up with the kids, hour for hour
choices.result: You match their hours for a month. Your body sends the bill.

events.text: {rookie}, from the academy, is invited to "observe" the bootcamp. He plays your role. He sits behind you during scrims and takes notes on your positions.

choices.text: Teach him everything. If he takes your seat, he will deserve it
choices.result: Management notices who the adult in the room is.

choices.text: Give him nothing and out-play him in every scrim

win.text: For two weeks you play like your seat is on fire. He goes back to the academy.

lose.text: In the mixed scrim, he wins the duel against you. Twice. Everyone saw.

events.text: A year after you refused the in-game leader role, the team's results are flat and your numbers keep sliding. The coach brings it up one last time: "The offer still stands. It will not stand next year."

choices.text: Swallow your pride and take the notebook
choices.result: A year late, but you get there. The team breathes out.

choices.text: No. You will go out with a rifle in your hands
choices.result: He nods slowly. You both know what that means.

events.text: A highlights channel posts "{name} in his prime". Two million views. The top comment: "What happened to this guy?"

choices.text: Share it: "Still here. Still annoying to play against."
choices.result: The scene has a soft spot for veterans who can laugh.

choices.text: Watch it alone, three times
choices.result: He was fast, that kid.

choices.text: Use it as fuel for one more big season

win.text: Your best month in two years. A new clip appears: "He is BACK."

lose.text: You push too hard and your hand pushes back.

events.text: {journalist} asks the question during a press conference: "Is this your last season?" The room goes quiet.

choices.text: "I will stop when the kids stop being afraid of me."
choices.result: It is on a T-shirt by the end of the week.

choices.text: "I honestly do not know."
choices.result: An honest answer. The article is kind.

choices.text: "Next question."
choices.result: The headline writes itself: "{name} dodges retirement question".
